# Volume 1 — CHAPTER XVII. A New Interest in Life

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

ON the following afternoon, as Nell leaned over her patchwork at the kitchen window, she chanced to look outside and saw Isolde standing near the Nymph’s Well, making mysterious signals to her. Immediately, Nell left the house and rushed down into the hollow, her lively eyes filled with a mixture of wonder and hope. However, that hope vanished as soon as she observed the despondent look on Isolde’s face.
{: #nw-v01-c17-p0000 }

“Hasn’t your mother yielded?” she gasped.
{: #nw-v01-c17-p0001 }

Sorrowfully, Isolde gave a shake of her head.
{: #nw-v01-c17-p0002 }

“No; and oh, Nell, she tells me I must not ever play with you anymore. I have wept and wept and I explained to her that you were not to blame, but it did not help. It took so much coaxing to get her permission for me to come down and bid you farewell. She stated that I could remain for merely ten minutes and she is using the clock to time me.”
{: #nw-v01-c17-p0003 }

“A decade of minutes is hardly enough time to bid a forever goodbye,” Nell uttered through her tears. “Oh, Isolde, will you give your solemn word to always remember me, your childhood companion, regardless of any closer companions who might embrace you?”
{: #nw-v01-c17-p0004 }

“Most certainly I shall,” wept Isolde, “and no other intimate friend will ever be mine—it is not my desire to possess one. Loving anyone else as deeply as I love you is impossible for me.”
{: #nw-v01-c17-p0005 }

“Oh, Isolde,” Nell exclaimed, folding her hands together, “do you love me?”
{: #nw-v01-c17-p0006 }

“Why, certainly I do. Were you unaware of that?”
{: #nw-v01-c17-p0007 }

“No.” Taking a deep breath, Nell said. “I assumed you held me in affection, naturally, but my hopes never reached your loving me. Why, Isolde, my belief was that no person was capable of loving me. Ever since the time I can recall, I have been loved by no one. Oh, how amazing this is! A beam of illumination has appeared, one that will perpetually illuminate the shadow of a road separated from thee, Isolde. Oh, utter it merely one more time.”
{: #nw-v01-c17-p0008 }

“You can be certain that my love for you, Nell, is devoted and will last forever,” Isolde declared firmly.
{: #nw-v01-c17-p0009 }

“And I shall forever hold thee dear, Isolde,” stated Nell, offering her hand in a serious manner. “Throughout the future, the thought of thee will gleam such as a star above my solitary existence, just as it is stated in that final tale we perused in company. Isolde, wilt thou grant me a strand of thy raven hair upon our farewell to cherish for all time?”
{: #nw-v01-c17-p0010 }

“Is there anything you can use to slice it?” asked Isolde, who dried the tears that Nell’s touching tone had prompted to stream once more, as she shifted her focus back to realistic matters.
{: #nw-v01-c17-p0011 }

“Yes. Fortunately, I have my patchwork scissors in the pocket of my apron,” Nell said. One of Isolde’s curls was solemnly clipped by her. “Farewell, my beloved friend. From now on, although we live next to one another, we must be like strangers. My heart, however, will always remain faithful to thee.”
{: #nw-v01-c17-p0012 }

Nell remained standing and observed Isolde until she was no longer visible, sorrowfully waving her hand toward her each time Isolde turned around to glance back. Afterward, she went back inside the house, temporarily comforted to no small degree by this imaginative farewell.
{: #nw-v01-c17-p0013 }

“Everything is ended,” she told Thirza. “Another friend will never be mine. My situation is actually more terrible than it was previously, since Lettie Marchant and Melisande are no longer with me. Even were they present, a change would have occurred. Little imaginary girls simply fail to fulfill you once you have known a genuine companion. Down beside the spring, Isolde and I shared a deeply moving goodbye. For the rest of my days, my memory will hold it sacred. Employing the most sorrowful phrasing I could imagine, I addressed her as ‘thou’ and ‘thee.’ Words like ‘thou’ and ‘thee’ appear far more poetic than ‘you.’ A lock of her hair was given to me by Isolde, which I plan to stitch inside a small pouch to hang about my neck for as long as I live. Be sure that it goes into the grave with me, because my life likely will not endure much longer. Maybe seeing me laid out frozen and deceased in her presence will cause Mrs. Pembroke to experience guilt over her actions, allowing Isolde to attend my burial.”
{: #nw-v01-c17-p0014 }

“I don’t think you are in any great danger of passing away from sorrow so long as your tongue keeps moving, Nell,” Thirza remarked without sympathy.
{: #nw-v01-c17-p0015 }

When the next Monday arrived, Nell caught Thirza off guard by descending from her bedroom, carrying her book basket supported by her arm and hip, her mouth drawn tight into a resolute expression.
{: #nw-v01-c17-p0016 }

“I will return to school,” she declared. “Since my companion has been so mercilessly ripped away from me, nothing else remains in my life. I am able to gaze upon her at school and reflect on bygone days.”
{: #nw-v01-c17-p0017 }

“You would do well to ponder your schoolwork and arithmetic,” Thirza remarked, hiding her happiness regarding how things were turning out. “Should you return to classes, my expectation is that we will not hear any further about smashing slates on folks’ heads or similar misbehavior. Conduct yourself properly and obey every instruction given by your educator.”
{: #nw-v01-c17-p0018 }

“I will attempt to be an exemplary student,” Nell assented mournfully. “I anticipate that it will not contain much enjoyment. Mr. Pidgeon stated that Posy Pullen was an exemplary student, and she possesses not a single trace of imagination or vitality. She is merely tedious and plodding, and she never appears to enjoy herself. However, I am feeling so downhearted that maybe I will find it simple at present. My route will be around by the road. Traveling via the Aspen Path entirely by myself is something I could not endure. Doing so would cause me to cry bitter tears.”
{: #nw-v01-c17-p0019 }

Everyone at school greeted Nell back with enthusiasm. During games, they had deeply missed her creativity, while her vocals were missed in the music, and her theatrical talent had been missed when books were read out loud at the dinner hour. While testament reading was taking place, Opal Pettigrew secretly passed three blue plums to her; Ella May MacKinnon presented her with a massive yellow pansy that had been excised from a floral catalogue's cover—a type of desk ornament highly valued at Brierley school. A proposal to instruct her in a truly exquisite new design of knit lace, which was very suitable for apron trimming, was made by Sophia Mott. A perfume bottle to hold slate water was given to her by Lettie Gammon, and on a sheet of light pink paper featuring scalloped edges, Julia Bell painstakingly transcribed this verse:
{: #nw-v01-c17-p0020 }

“TO NELL
{: #nw-v01-c17-p0021 }

“As evening pulls its veil across And secures it with a star Keep in mind you possess a friend Even if she should roam afar.”
{: #nw-v01-c17-p0022 }

“To have one's worth recognized feels truly wonderful,” Nell murmured delightedly to Thirza later that evening.
{: #nw-v01-c17-p0023 }

Female students were not the sole pupils who “appreciated” her. Upon returning to her desk following the dinner hour—Mr. Pidgeon had directed her to share a seat with the exemplary Posy Pullen—she discovered a large, mouth-watering “strawberry apple” lying there. Nell snatched it up, fully prepared to bite into it, until it occurred to her that the sole location in Brierley producing strawberry apples was the ancient Carrow orchard situated across the Lake of Glassy Waters. Nell let the apple fall as though it were a piece of burning coal and conspicuously cleaned her hands using her handkerchief. The apple remained undisturbed upon her desk through to the following day, at which time young Timothy Pullen, whose duties included sweeping the schoolhouse and lighting the fire, claimed it as part of his earned benefits. Wilfred Mott’s slate pencil, magnificently decorated in banded red and yellow paper, priced at two cents whereas normal pencils were priced at merely one, which he passed along to her following the dinner hour, received a far more approving response. Nell was kindly inclined to take it and compensated the giver with a smile that instantly elevated that enamored boy into the seventh heaven of joy, leading him to commit such terrible mistakes during his dictation that Mr. Pidgeon forced him to stay behind after school to write it again.
{: #nw-v01-c17-p0024 }

However since,
{: #nw-v01-c17-p0025 }

When Brutus’s bust was missing from Cæsar’s procession, it served only to bring Rome’s finest son even more to her mind,
{: #nw-v01-c17-p0026 }

Thus, because Isolde Pembroke, who occupied a seat beside Tibby Tulk, noticeably failed to offer any tribute or acknowledgment, Nell’s modest victory was rendered bitter.
{: #nw-v01-c17-p0027 }

“I think Isolde may have offered me a single smile,” she lamented to Thirza when evening came. Yet as the following morning arrived, Nell received a tiny package alongside a letter that had been folded and twisted in the most extraordinary and terrifying manner.
{: #nw-v01-c17-p0028 }

“My dear Nell,” read the first, “it is Mother’s instruction that I must neither play with you nor speak to you, even at school. You must not be angry with me, as it is not my doing, for my love for you remains as strong as ever. Without you to hear all my secrets, I miss you terribly, and Tibby Tulk is not to my liking at all. I crafted a new bookmarker for you using red tissue paper. These are extremely popular currently, with a mere three girls in school possessing the skill to construct them. As your eyes fall upon it, keep in mind
{: #nw-v01-c17-p0029 }

Your genuine companion, Isolde Pembroke.
{: #nw-v01-c17-p0030 }

Having perused the message, Nell bestowed a kiss upon the bookmark and sent a swift answer back across the school grounds.
{: #nw-v01-c17-p0031 }

My own darling Isolde:— Naturally, I am not angry with you for needing to comply with your mother's wishes. Our souls are able to communicate. I will preserve your beautiful gift eternally. Posy Pullen is an exceedingly pleasant small girl—even though she lacks imagination—however, having served as Isolde’s busum friend, I am unable to become Posy’s. Kindly pardon any errors since my spelling remains somewhat imperfect, even if greatly improoved.
{: #nw-v01-c17-p0032 }

Ever yours to the end of life, Nell or Lucinda Harcourt.
{: #nw-v01-c17-p0033 }

P.S. Tonight, I will rest with your letter beneath my pillow.
{: #nw-v01-c17-p0034 }

A. or C.S.
{: #nw-v01-c17-p0035 }

Thirza harbored gloomy anticipations of fresh difficulties now that Nell was attending school once more. However, no trouble materialized. It may be that Posy Pullen’s “model” attitude influenced Nell; in any case, her relationship with Mr. Pidgeon remained quite smooth from that time on. Throwing her whole heart and soul into her academic work, she was resolved that Hugh Carrow would not surpass her in a single subject. The competition that arose between the two soon became obvious; while Hugh’s participation was completely friendly, it is greatly to be doubted that Nell felt the same way, as she indisputably possessed an undesirable tendency to harbor animosity. The intensity of her dislikes matched the intensity of her affections. She refused to demean herself by confessing an intention to compete against Hugh in her studies, as doing so would amount to recognizing his existence, which Nell resolutely refused to do; nevertheless, the contest persisted with academic achievements shifting back and forth between them. At one moment, Hugh occupied the top spot in spelling; at the next, Nell, tossing her long red braids, successfully spelled him down. On a particular morning, Hugh completed every sum without error and earned a place on the honor roll on the blackboard; on the following morning, Nell, having engaged in a frantic struggle with decimals throughout the previous night, took top honors. On one terrible occasion, they achieved identical scores and had their names posted side by side. The humiliation for Nell was nearly equal to that of a published marriage notice, and her embarrassment was just as obvious as Hugh’s delight. Every month, when the written tests were administered, the resulting tension was agonizing. During the initial month, Hugh finished three points in front. During the second, Nell surpassed him by five points. Yet her victory lost its sweetness because Hugh openly offered her his enthusiastic congratulations in front of all the students. Victory would have brought her far greater joy if he had experienced the bitterness of his failure.
{: #nw-v01-c17-p0036 }

A pupil whose resolve to learn was as unwavering as Nell's could scarcely avoid advancing under any instructor, even if Mr. Pidgeon was perhaps not a particularly effective one. Nell and Hugh had each been advanced to the fifth class when the term concluded, and they were permitted to commence their studies in the fundamentals of “the branches”—a term that referred to Latin, geometry, French, and algebra. It was in geometry that Nell suffered her ultimate defeat.
{: #nw-v01-c17-p0037 }

“It’s completely terrible material, Thirza,” she moaned. “I’m certain I will not ever manage to understand it. There isn't any room for imagination in it whatsoever. Mr. Pidgeon tells me I am the biggest blockhead he has ever seen with it. And Hughie—that is to say certain of the rest are so clever with it. It is deeply humiliating, Thirza.”
{: #nw-v01-c17-p0038 }

“Isolde manages even better than I manage. However, I have no objection to Isolde outdoing me. Even though our meetings are as strangers now, my love for her remains one that cannot be extinguished. Thinking of her causes me great sadness on occasion. Nevertheless, Thirza, a person is unable to remain sad for very long when the world is this interesting, isn't that so?”
{: #nw-v01-c17-p0039 }
